reviews.author: Carpe Diem
reviews.text: I visited with some skepticism because the Korean bingsoo shop had closed down, but I was surprised by how delicious it was. It was a shame the pistachio flavor was sold out, but I will definitely visit again to try it next time.

reviews.author: Harris Hakimi
reviews.text: My go-to bingsu place!!! LOVE IT SO SO MUCH. flavours are immaculate and the prices are affordable, sesuai bawak family and friends! The staffs are friendly and lovely, just that kena makan for just 1hour to make way for other customers, understandable so yeah. Recommended!

reviews.author: Jin
reviews.text: We tried the roasted soybean oolong and it was superb! One of the nicest bingsu I had. Soft and flavorful with well and tasteful sides and cheese to add on to your liking. Clean and bright interior. Will be back!

reviews.author: mugsey
reviews.text: Sooo good! Best bingsu ever! Love the pistachio one so much (not pictured) I think it was their most recent menu. They used real pistachio nuts for the toppings for that one, yum!! We came late at around 10 pm actually but had to queue for a while, so it was really packed when we arrived. No wonder la because they’re really good 👏

reviews.author: Jac Yim
reviews.text:
Brought here by a friend. Ordered the best seller oolong soybean, mango sago and Thai milk tea.
The oolong soybean was nice. Mango is a little sweet for us. The highlight for me is the Thai milk tea. I really love the combination. Nicely finely shaved ice with onde onde glutinous squares, topped with crushed biscoff, and bubble coconut fillings. Absolutely delicious! A must try if you come here.

reviews.author: Ohaiyo Simidaa
reviews.text:
The bingsu here is good. We tried the soybean and pistachio flavours, and both were rich, thick, and very tasty. You can choose two add-ons, and I highly recommend adding the chocolate butter crisps — they enhance the flavour and add a nice crunch to the bingsu.

Prices start from around RM24 and above for a bowl of bingsu, which is generous enough to be shared by two people.

The environment is slightly warm, and the interior design is quite simple. Overall, it’s a nice spot for dessert, especially if you’re coming mainly for the bingsu rather than the ambience.

reviews.author: Jeffrey Kok
reviews.text: Really delicious and refreshing bingsu. The shop has a nice minimalist vibe, but it is quite small, so it feels a bit tight when it’s crowded. Great for a fast chill-out session!

reviews.author: CW Wong
reviews.text:
Good desert place for bingsu. Well portioned and good price point!

We had the peach oolong one. The ice is fluffy and so soft, but well flavoured. Had no idea how to eat so wife poured the toppings on the mountain of ice and some fell on the floor 🙀

However this outlet had a strange smell, like something rotting. It made us not want to linger too long.
